title: Can Sun-Faded Hardwood Floors Under Rugs Be Fixed?
meta: Yes: a rug shadow on sun-faded hardwood is fixed by a full sand and refinish at $3.99 per sq ft, not a recoat. Kirkland examples and costs, Wills Flooring.
keywords: sun faded hardwood floors under rug, rug shadow on hardwood floor fix, hardwood floor discoloration from sunlight, refinish sun damaged wood floors, hardwood floor refinishing Kirkland WA

blocks.lead: Yes. A rug shadow on hardwood is fixed by sanding the whole floor to bare wood and refinishing it, which costs $3.99 per sq ft at Wills Flooring. A screen and recoat will not remove it.
blocks.detail: Sunlight changes the color of both the finish and the top fraction of a millimeter of wood, so the fade has to be sanded off, not coated over. The exceptions are exotic species that keep changing and floors too thin to sand.

blocks.html: Pull up an area rug in a west-facing Kirkland living room after five years and there it is: a sharp rectangle of darker floor inside a sea of lighter, yellower wood. Houghton and Juanita homes with big windows toward Lake Washington get this worse than anywhere else we work, because afternoon sun comes in low and hard for hours. The question we get on the phone is always the same. Can it be fixed without replacing the floor? Almost always yes. Here is why it happens, what actually removes it and what it costs.

items.title: UV changes the wood itself
items.text: Ultraviolet light breaks down lignin in the top layer of wood. Most domestic species lighten and yellow; cherry and many exotics darken. The change is only skin deep, a fraction of a millimeter, which is exactly why sanding removes it.

items.title: The finish ambers too
items.text: Oil-based polyurethane turns amber with light and age. Older Kirkland floors from the 1980s and 90s often have three or four coats of it, and the uncovered area goes orange while the rug keeps its patch pale and original.

items.title: Species decides how bad it gets
items.text: Red oak shifts a little. Maple and fir yellow noticeably. Brazilian cherry, tigerwood and other exotics can move several shades in a single summer. White oak with a water-based finish is the most stable combination we install.

items.title: Kirkland windows make it worse
items.text: Lakefront and view lots in Houghton, Juanita and Finn Hill face west or southwest on purpose. Low evening sun through big glass is the strongest UV a floor sees. North-facing rooms in Rose Hill rarely show a shadow at all.

blocks.text: Recoat or sand: which one removes the fade

a.title: Removes the shadow
items: Takes the floor to bare wood, past the discolored layer
Whole floor goes back to one even color
Three coats of Bona water-based finish, which resists ambering
Chance to change sheen or add stain at $6.50 / sq ft
Fixes scratches and dull spots at the same time

b.title: Locks the shadow in
items: Only abrades the top of the existing finish
The color difference is under the finish and in the wood, so it stays
Fresh clear coat can make the contrast more visible
Right for a dull but even floor, wrong for a two-tone one
Many companies sell it anyway because it is a fast day

blocks.text: When sanding will not fully fix it

items: The floor is Brazilian cherry, tigerwood or another photosensitive exotic. Sanding evens it out today, but the wood keeps darkening for years, so the next rug will leave the next shadow. Stain and UV film slow it; nothing stops it.
The floor is engineered with a wear layer under 2 mm. There is not enough wood to sand past the faded layer safely. We measure the veneer at an exposed edge before quoting.
The solid floor has already been sanded four or more times and the tongue is close to the surface. Sanding thin boards risks nail heads and splintered edges.
The fade is not fade. Gray or black areas under a rug near a door or a plant are usually moisture, not sun. Those are a different fix and sometimes a board replacement.
Someone has already recoated over the shadow with an oil-based finish. It still sands out, but expect an extra pass and a little more time on the invoice.

blocks.title: Do not spot-sand the rectangle:
blocks.text: A common DIY thread suggests sanding only the dark patch to match the rest. It does not work. The surrounding wood is already at its faded color and the patch will fade to a different tone on its own schedule, so you end up with a blurry rectangle instead of a sharp one. The only even result is the whole floor sanded and finished together.
How to keep the new floor from shadowing again

items.html: Put UV film on the west and south glass. Modern clear window film blocks most ultraviolet without tinting the view of the lake. It is the single most effective step for Kirkland view homes.
Rotate or lift the rugs seasonally. Move the rug a foot, or roll it up for a few weeks each summer so the covered area catches up. Boring, but it works.

Choose a water-based finish. Bona water-based finishes stay clear instead of ambering, so at least the finish half of the problem goes away. Wills uses three coats as standard, and we are Bona Certified Craftsmen.
Consider a light stain on light woods. A pale stain on maple or oak masks small tone shifts better than a natural finish does. Pick it from real samples in your own light at the free estimate.
Use breathable rug pads. Solid rubber pads trap moisture and can leave their own marks. A felt or open-weave pad lets the floor breathe and is kinder to the finish.
Remember the warranty covers workmanship, not sunlight. Our 1-year workmanship warranty covers the sanding and finish. No finish stops UV. Prevention is on the homeowner, and it is not hard.

faq.q: Will the rug shadow fade on its own if I remove the rug?
faq.a: Partly, and slowly. The dark patch will lighten toward the rest of the floor over months to years, but the finish around it keeps ambering too, so the two rarely meet. On oak you may get close enough to live with. On maple, fir or exotics the difference usually stays visible until the floor is sanded.

faq.q: Can I fix sun-faded hardwood without sanding?
faq.a: Not reliably. Recoating locks the difference in, and spot sanding creates a blurred patch. Some people hide it with a darker stain applied over a light sand, but stain over old finish is uneven. A full sand to bare wood is the only fix that gives one even color.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fix sun-faded floors in Kirkland?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates it is a standard refinish: $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish or $6.50 with stain, 500 sq ft minimum. A 700 sq ft Kirkland living and dining area costs $2,793 natural, or $4,550 stained. Stairs, dust containment and appliance moves are extra.

faq.q: Do engineered hardwood floors fade under rugs too?
faq.a: Yes, the veneer is real wood and fades like solid. Whether it can be fixed depends on wear layer thickness. Veneers of 3 mm or more can usually take one careful sanding. Under 2 mm, we recommend UV film and rug rotation instead, or replacement if the contrast bothers you.

faq.q: Does a darker stain prevent sun fade?
faq.a: It hides it better rather than preventing it. Pigment in stain absorbs some UV and evens out tone differences, so a medium-brown floor shows a shadow far less than a natural maple floor. The wood underneath still changes; you just cannot see it as easily.

faq.q: How long does the refinish take with a Kirkland family living at home?
faq.a: Three to four days for a natural finish on a typical main floor, four to five with stain. You can walk in socks after 24 hours and set rugs back down after two weeks, once the finish has fully cured. Dust containment at $250 is worth it if you stay in the house.
